source_text: Solum esse in omnibus animalibus, cui superiores mandibulas moveri Albinus affirmat; et ignem, cum sit omnibus exitio, salamandrae esse ludibrio Naturalia per accidens non converti parentes in filios ea quae non habent ipsi non posse transfundere
pass_a_gloss: Only to-be in to-all animalibus, to-whom higher mandibulas moveri Albinus affirmat; and ignem, when/with may-be to-all exitio, salamandrae to-be ludibrio natural through something-added not converti parents in sons she/it which not have themselves not to-be-able transfundere.
pass_b_english: Albinus affirms that among all animals the crocodile alone moves its upper jaws; and fire, though destructive to everything else, is a plaything for the salamander.
Natural characteristics are not changed by an accidental occurrence.
A parent cannot transmit to offspring what the parent does not possess.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
